http://www.bgnes.com/politics/three-part.text: The National Liberal Party (PNL), the Save Romania Union (USR) and the Democratic Alliance of Hungarians in Romania (UDMR) have drawn up an initial version of the future cabinet led by prime minister-designate Siegfried Muresan, Digi24 reported. The leaders of the three parties have not yet reached a final agreement, with negotiations focused mainly on ministries that were controlled by the Social Democratic Party (PSD) until the spring. According to Digi24, the parties are disputing portfolios including energy, health, justice and transport. The PNL is expected to receive seven ministries, the USR six and the UDMR three. During talks at Victoria Palace on September 23, the leaders decided that each party would keep the ministries it currently controls, most likely with the same ministers. The distribution of the portfolios previously controlled by the PSD has yet to be finalized. Negotiations have stalled over these ministries, as the parties are seeking control of those considered more important. According to Digi24, the PNL wants the Ministry of Energy, the Ministry of Health or the Ministry of Justice. The USR is also seeking the Justice Ministry, as well as the Ministry of Transport. The UDMR wants to retain three ministries but is pushing for more significant portfolios. Its representatives would like to replace the Ministry of Culture with the Ministry of Agriculture and also obtain either the Ministry of Health or the Ministry of Transport. Regarding the structure of the future government, Ilie Bolojan, Dominic Fritz and Kelemen Hunor agreed that there should be three deputy prime ministers instead of the current five. All deputy prime ministers will also serve as ministers, meaning no additional posts will be created for people outside the government. Each ministry will also have a maximum of three state secretaries. | BGNES
